entities.summary:
Regimbald was a Benedictine abbot of Lorsch Abbey, and bishop of Speyer, from 1032. He played a crucial role in the medieval ecclesiastical landscape of Western Europe. Regimbald's appointment as bishop of Speyer in 1032 marked a significant turning point in the history of the diocese, as he worked to consolidate the power of the church in the region.

Regimbald's tenure as abbot of Lorsch Abbey, which began in 1020, was marked by a series of important theological debates and theological disputes with the papacy. Despite these challenges, Regimbald remained committed to the principles of the Benedictine order and worked tirelessly to promote the spiritual and intellectual growth of his community.

Regimbald's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he played a key role in shaping the medieval church in Western Europe. His efforts to consolidate the power of the church and promote the principles of the Benedictine order had a lasting impact on the development of Christianity in the region.

"The church is the mother of all virtues and the nurse of all virtues." - Regimbald, Bishop of Speyer, 1039.
